newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan slams U.S. military aid to African countries.
newsitem.headline: Sudan slams U.S. military aid to African countries.

text.p: Sudan's parliament has denounced the United States, accusing it of providing its African neighbours with military aid to use against Khartoum.

The official SUNA news agency said on Wednesday that parliament on Tuesday denounced the "hostile practices of the U.S. against Sudan and its incitement of the neighbouring countries against it" and "extending military aid to the neighbouring regimes, particularly Eritrea and Ethiopia, and urging them overtly to interfere in Sudan's internal affairs."
The United States said on Tuesday it was sending military aid to Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda but denied it was assisting them in a bid to help overthrow Sudan's Islamic regime.
State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said in Washington it was "nonlethal defensive military assistance".

Sudan also condemned United Nations resolution 1070, which the world body on August 16 imposed on Sudan but delayed putting into effect for at least three months depending on a U.N. report on whether Khartoum was complying with the council's demands.

The sanctions, which include air, diplomatic and travel embargoes, target Sudan for its failure to extradite three Egyptians accused of taking part in a plot to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Ethiopia last year.
Sudan says the three are not in the country.
"The use of U.N. organs to settle political accounts represents a stark example of the disregard of norms and values governing international relations," the parliament said.
It also attacked Egypt, accusing it of a plot targeting Sudan's unity.
